title: Weird science project
description: A student’s science project is getting out of control

pitches.title: The Extra Credit Ecosystem
pitches.text: A student's sealed terrarium grows trees overnight, then starts producing tiny versions of the school staff. Watching a miniature principal expel a beetle reveals that the ecosystem copies whatever its observer believes deserves authority. When its roots spread into classrooms, the investigators stop trying to dominate it and convince the student to study cooperation instead. The miniature staff form a functioning society, thoroughly embarrassing their full-size counterparts.

pitches.title: The Volcano That Remembers
pitches.adjustment: The project is a model volcano.
pitches.text: Each eruption spits out an object from a different vanished civilization. The investigators identify fresh fingerprints on supposedly ancient artifacts and discover that the volcano is disgorging the possessions of people currently falling through time. Its baking-soda chamber has opened a prehistoric fault in causality. They reverse the classroom demonstration, retrieve the displaced students, and leave history with one inexplicable plastic participation trophy.

pitches.title: Control Group
pitches.text: The student's plant-growth experiment makes one classroom impossibly cheerful while the untreated class develops identical nightmares. Interviewing both groups reveals an invisible animal that eats distress and stores it elsewhere, attracted by the experimental fertilizer. Killing it would release weeks of concentrated misery. The investigators coax it into eating a horror-movie marathon, then relocate it to an abandoned cinema where consenting enthusiasts provide a sustainable diet.

pitches.title: Better Than the Original
pitches.text: A homemade cloning apparatus duplicates a hamster, a sandwich, then the student's father. The duplicate father is more attentive, and every copied object begins outlasting its original. Examination shows that the machine summons idealized beings from the student's wishful imagination, slowly replacing the real world. The investigators make the student confront what the perfect father cannot remember, breaking the fantasy's authority and leaving the original family to have an awkward necessary conversation.

pitches.title: The Sun in the Shoebox
pitches.text: A student trying to win the energy category builds a miniature sun that answers questions in their missing grandfather's voice. Its increasing heat follows questions about death, not electrical input. The grandfather is trapped inside a newborn star, and every remembered regret accelerates its growth. The team helps him admit that his grandchild owes him no grand achievement; he releases the star into space before it consumes the gym.

pitches.title: Late Results
pitches.text: A student's prediction engine prints tomorrow's science-fair results, including several deaths. The investigators find that predictions change whenever someone reads them: an anxious future version of the student is manufacturing disasters to prevent one fatal experiment. With no reliable expert coming, they send a plain description of the actual wiring fault through the apparatus. The future student stops escalating, and the unremarkable repaired project wins nothing but everybody survives.

pitches.title: Homegrown Gravity
pitches.text: A student's gravity experiment leaves the gym floating above town, tethered only by extension cords. Falling objects rise toward a transparent creature wrapped around the building. The apparatus has mistaken a spacefaring filter-feeder for a gravitational field and keeps feeding it electricity. The investigators cut power selectively, lure it toward a substation's harmless static plume, and land the gym on the parking lot while teachers insist attendance still counts.

pitches.title: The Mold Knows
pitches.text: A bread-mold project starts spelling accurate allegations about teachers, then grows accusations into living scenes. Checking one scene reveals that the organism is reconstructing buried memories from shed skin cells, including a student's suppressed account of a real assault. The team preserves that testimony before drying out the mold, whose expanding reenactments threaten to overwrite the school. The culprit faces ordinary consequences, and the student finally gets credit for observant science.

pitches.title: Peer Review
pitches.text: The student's radio project receives meticulous corrections from voices inside the static. Their improved device summons a towering visitor who announces the experiment has failed ethical review. The voices were juvenile aliens cheating on their own assignment by recruiting a human partner. The investigators expose both sides' copied work and negotiate a joint remedial project: safely dismantling the portal. Nobody wins a ribbon, but the visiting evaluator gives the entire planet another chance.

pitches.title: Growing Pains
pitches.text: A student invents a serum that makes seedlings mature instantly; its spilled runoff ages the nearby neighborhood. Growth rings reveal that the plants borrow years from whatever tends them, and the student has unknowingly given decades of life to a dying orchard. The investigators graft the trees back into the experiment's original seedling, returning the stolen years. The now-ancient sapling becomes a temperamental houseplant that demands retirement before its owner graduates.

title: Weird tracks
description: Unusual tracks are being found in the woods

pitches.title: Footprints Before Feet
pitches.text: Enormous prints appear at sunrise, but cameras show no creature making them. Their route leads toward a missing child's house, and the depth increases as searchers lose hope. They belong to the protective giant the child imagined while lost; it is walking backward through time to find its creator. The investigators follow tomorrow's tracks today, rescue the child, and persuade the giant to stop before its worried footsteps flatten the neighborhood.

pitches.title: The Forest Walks Out
pitches.text: Tracks resemble animal paws until soil samples show every footprint contains an entire uprooted tree. Logging records match the trail: the forest is growing legs to flee a proposed development, taking campers with it. The team locates its slow-moving heart and removes the trapped people, then redirects the migration through an abandoned industrial site. The developer arrives to clear land and discovers his new headquarters has become a very opinionated woodland.

pitches.title: Borrowed Shoes
pitches.text: Tracks switch between deer, bare feet, and expensive hiking boots without changing stride. Interviews uncover a shapeshifter lending different bodies to injured animals, but losing track of who belongs where. Predators now inhabit human forms and frightened hikers have antlers. The investigators reconstruct the exchanges from mud samples and arrange a chaotic reunion around the original spring. Everybody gets their body back, except a poacher whose deer victim declines the trade.

pitches.title: Prints from Below
pitches.text: Upside-down tracks appear on roots and the undersides of fallen logs. A survey reveals a second forest occupying the same space with gravity reversed, and an exhausted ranger is walking its ceiling to signal for help. The overlap widens whenever machinery vibrates the bedrock. The investigators shut down a nearby quarry, pull the ranger through a hollow stump, and seal the resonance with ordinary gravel while the quarry invoices them for interruption.

pitches.title: The Last Mammoth
pitches.text: Mammoth prints circle the woods, although no animal is seen and nearby freezers fail overnight. A preserved tusk recently thawed in a private collection is rebuilding its owner from absorbed cold. The resurrecting animal seeks its herd, freezing campers into mistaken companions. The investigators locate the herd's fossil bed and reunite the tusk with it. Winter withdraws, leaving one brief living mammoth farewell and several thoroughly ruined picnic lunches.

pitches.title: Almost Human
pitches.text: Strange prints follow hikers home but always stop one pace short of the door. A trail camera captures a boneless creature rehearsing human movement by studying discarded shoes. It wants to become human, and its attempted handshakes crush furniture and bones. The investigators offer a mannequin as a safe body template, then teach it boundaries at an empty campground. It becomes a competent campsite host with disturbingly flexible elbows and genuine pride in its first paycheck.

pitches.title: The Hunt That Already Happened
pitches.text: The prints match a supposedly extinct predator and contain bullets fired decades apart. Each damaged track leads to a hunter who dies in an old hunting accident. A ghost animal is replaying its deaths through everyone who inherited its trophies. The investigators gather the scattered remains and give the creature an unclaimed grave, ending the hunt. One collector refuses his skull; he becomes the final trophy instead, neatly completing the creature's collection.

pitches.title: Tracks to Nowhere
pitches.text: Every set of bizarre tracks ends beside an ordinary puddle, and boots left overnight come back wet with seawater. The puddles connect to an island where an amphibious people have been rescuing hikers they mistake for stranded land fish. Their helpful retrieval patrols are emptying the forest. The team visits the island, negotiates the return of the bewildered hikers, and distributes reflective boundary markers that mean 'we live here, unfortunately.'

pitches.title: Walking Wounds
pitches.text: The prints bleed sap and change shape near places where hikers were injured. Following them reveals a creature made from all the forest's abandoned pain, desperately searching for whoever can take it away. The team's attempted exorcism makes every old wound reopen. They instead help local survivors publicly acknowledge what happened and stop hiding their scars; the creature shrinks into a small limping fox, which finally finds a den and rests.

pitches.title: The Shortcut Animal
pitches.text: The tracks connect places miles apart, and following them cuts a two-hour hike to thirty seconds while stealing hours from someone elsewhere. A startled deer has eaten fruit from a tree rooted outside time. The investigators track the lost hours to a commuter slowly dying of accelerated age. They capture the deer without following its prints and feed it ordinary bitter bark, returning the borrowed time and restoring its boringly inconvenient normal commute.

title: Strange gigs
description: An app is offering good money for very strange work

pitches.title: Professional Mourner
pitches.text: The app pays workers to attend funerals for people who are still alive. The investigators accept a shift and notice each funeral erases its subject from photographs. The platform is a death spirit buying counterfeit public mourning to make premature deaths legitimate. They crash its largest booking with the supposedly deceased clients, converting the ceremony into a birthday party. The victims return, and the spirit must refund every fraudulent funeral in genuinely excellent currency.

pitches.title: Someone Has to Hold It
pitches.text: High-paying gigs ask workers to stand in an alley holding an invisible handle. Injuries and vanished replacements lead the team to an ancient jail whose door exists only when held shut by human attention. The founder automated recruitment after all its original keepers died. Inside waits a creature that eats loneliness. The investigators stop staffing isolated shifts, bring the workers together, and open the door; surrounded by solidarity, the starving prisoner collapses into harmless dust.

pitches.title: Surge Pricing for Souls
pitches.text: Workers earn fortunes delivering warm paper bags, then discover their friends no longer recognize them. Thermal imaging shows a small human silhouette in each bag: the app pays by selling the courier's future relationships to lonely demons. The investigators intercept a delivery reunion, where the buyers have become dependent on borrowed affection. They force the founder to surrender his own network of stolen connections, freeing the couriers but leaving him rich, alive, and completely forgotten.

pitches.title: Night Gardener
pitches.text: The best gigs involve watering weeds in pavement cracks at 3 a.m. The weeds bloom into miniature doors, and missing couriers appear inside them as sleeping gardeners. An underground civilization is cultivating routes to evacuate its collapsing world but regards temporary workers as seed stock. The investigators use the app to organize an above-ground rescue corridor, bring the gardeners home, and demand the refugees pay actual wages rather than propagate humans again.

pitches.title: Last Shift
pitches.text: The app assigns tiny pointless errands that coincide with avoided accidents: moving a chair, delaying a bus, spilling coffee. The team discovers its anonymous dispatcher is a future investigator trying to avert the agency's destruction. Each successful task transfers the fatal disaster to another worker. Rather than keep sacrificing replacements, they collectively refuse the final gig and evacuate its target. The future dispatcher disappears, leaving a saved neighborhood and an ominously empty support line.

pitches.title: Stand-In
pitches.text: Workers are paid to sit at family dinners wearing supplied clothes, while everyone insists they are a returning relative. The app connects bereaved households to an entity that edits strangers into missing people's lives. As the assignments lengthen, couriers lose their original identities. The investigators make a host family name the person they truly lost and the worker they are exploiting. That honest double acknowledgment breaks the substitution, turning the other fake reunions into equally difficult real farewells.

pitches.title: Five Stars or Else
pitches.text: Customers rate workers with bizarre complaints: insufficient terror, weak screaming, disappointing transformation. A disgruntled courier's video reveals jobs are live performances for creatures that mistake human life for interactive entertainment. The app's founder is a captive actor advertising Earth to buy his freedom. The team fakes a disastrous planetary finale, sabotages audience confidence, and gets the feed canceled. Freed workers keep their earnings; the founder receives one final brutally accurate performance review.

pitches.title: House Sitting for Nobody
pitches.text: The app pays investigators to occupy empty houses and prevent anyone saying their address aloud. They find matching blueprints and hear streets shifting overnight: a migrating predator disguises its teeth as rental properties, using residents as ballast. Occupied houses hold it in place until it can swallow a suburb. The team coordinates a simultaneous checkout through the app, starving the trap of occupants and forcing the monster to leave town with several deeply confused property investors aboard.

pitches.title: The Currency Is Real
pitches.text: Strange shifts pay in coins that buy anything once, but purchases vanish when the coins change hands again. The investigators trace the money to a faerie market exporting its unstable economy into town. Ordinary shops begin exchanging customers' memories instead of goods. They locate the broker, convert the remaining magical currency into one communal purchase of the market's exit gate, and return the coins. Their payment is a gate nobody can pawn and a rescued local economy.

pitches.title: Replacement Heaven
pitches.text: The jobs ask people to comfort exhausted strangers, wash muddy dogs, and fix broken toys; each worker briefly glows afterward. The investigators discover angels have deserted a malfunctioning afterlife, outsourcing small mercies through an app built by a dead programmer. Closing it would strand the dead and erase the living workers' unexpected purpose. They expose its supernatural ownership, require consent, and establish a modest human-run support service, despite headquarters being unable to supply so much as a printer.

title: Overly difficult escape room
description: The local escape room has an unusual design

pitches.title: The Room Is Escaping
pitches.text: The investigators find the escape room's walls crawling toward an exit while customers are plastered into place. Scratches under the paint reveal a captive architectural creature whose keeper sold its struggling movements as puzzles. Freeing it seems likely to crush everybody. The team uncouples the decorative rooms, shows the creature how to shed its outer shell, and leads the customers out through its abandoned skin. The owner is left running an unusually candid demolition attraction.

pitches.title: Solved by the Wrong Person
pitches.text: Every solution opens the door for one player and locks another deeper inside. Old booking records show the design is reenacting a mining rescue in which survivors blamed the youngest worker for their own cowardice. The trapped worker's ghost demands someone accept responsibility without selecting a substitute victim. The investigators reconstruct the abandonment and have the surviving organizer publicly confess. The doors open together, and an attraction built on a lie becomes a painfully honest memorial.

pitches.title: The Exit Is a Customer
pitches.text: Missing players appear later as enthusiastic staff with no memory of arriving. A body scan reveals each solved puzzle removes a small piece of personal history, constructing an ideal employee from the remainder. The escape room is an organism that digests identities into attendants. The investigators scatter contradictory memories through its clue system, giving the attendants back their inconvenient selves. They flee while the confused organism interviews its owner for the position of permanent snack.

pitches.title: An Hour Forever
pitches.text: The room resets at sixty minutes, but the investigators' bruises and hunger persist. A terrified designer appears in reflections, trapped since using stolen time magic to perfect the customer experience. Each reset borrows an hour from nearby hospital patients. The team deliberately breaks the final puzzle before the timer ends, destroying the demand for a perfect run. Everyone exits into a single messy hour, including the designer, who now owes years of actual restitution.

pitches.title: The Unfinished Door
pitches.text: The most difficult room has no puzzles, only a painted door customers insist they can almost remember opening. Beneath it lies a doorway removed from every participant's childhood dream by the same therapist. An escaped dream predator has rebuilt that suppressed exit as bait. The investigators recover the dreams, recognize the predator's comforting disguise, and draw a genuinely different door together. They leave through their own creation, trapping the creature in its recycled invitation.

pitches.title: Emergency Exit
pitches.text: The owner insists the escape room is safe, yet the fire exit leads to a burning version of town. Records show each visitor is being tested by an angel rehearsing who deserves rescue during an imminent catastrophe. The investigators discover that its rigid test kills cooperative groups because sacrifice appears as failure. They rescue the angel's own trapped assistant, demonstrating an outcome it excluded. Shamed into revising its judgment, it stops the catastrophe rather than grading the victims.

pitches.title: Puzzle Parasite
pitches.text: Players emerge brilliantly clever and unable to decide anything without finding a clue. A living pattern embedded in the room teaches minds to view all reality as one puzzle, multiplying every time a solution feels satisfying. The investigators notice the pattern cannot process an unnecessary act of kindness. They abandon the elaborate clues, comfort a frightened stranger, and walk through an ordinary unlocked door. The parasite loses its grip; its designer is devastated by the terrible customer feedback.

pitches.title: Build Your Own Captor
pitches.text: Players assemble a helpful robot from parts earned at each stage, then disappear after finishing. The 'robot' is a dismembered demon commissioning its own resurrection from paying volunteers. The investigators recognize body parts concealed as novelty components and find previous teams alive inside its unfinished stomach. They complete only its mouth, bargain for the prisoners with the withheld limbs, then scatter the pieces among incompatible recycling streams. The demon gets a very limited customer-service career.

pitches.title: The Room Nobody Booked
pitches.text: The booking confirmation lists eleven players, though only ten arrived; clues repeatedly require the missing eleventh. A ghost escaped into the reservation system after dying unnoticed during an early trial run. It traps groups until someone notices its absence as a person rather than a numerical inconvenience. The team finds its identity in a neglected emergency contact field, calls its family, and holds an improvised remembrance. The final lock opens with no puzzle answer at all.

pitches.title: Exit Interview
pitches.adjustment: The attraction includes a mock workplace.
pitches.text: The office-themed escape room asks participants to resign, but each resignation transfers them to a monstrous version of their real workplace. The owner trapped a demon of obligation and accidentally built it a recruitment funnel. Reading participants' desperate notes shows it cannot bind someone who chooses a responsibility freely. The investigators agree to rescue one another without promising lifetime service, breaking the funnel and returning everyone. The exit survey still demands a reason for leaving.

title: Weird abandoned building
description: Investigators requested to a local abandoned building

pitches.title: The Building Nobody Misses
pitches.text: An abandoned apartment block contains fresh meals and residents whom nobody outside remembers. The team finds these are people gradually erased when their last relationships ended; the building has been sheltering them, at the cost of forgetting itself. Demolition would erase every resident permanently. The investigators reconnect one tenant with an estranged sister, then organize introductions for the rest. The block reappears on city maps and immediately receives years of backdated bills.

pitches.title: Open House for the Dead
pitches.text: A realtor requests help when an abandoned house stages itself differently every night. Investigators find ghosts auditioning the rooms for a family they intend to replace, competing with glossy visions of domestic perfection. The house itself has been lonely since a fatal eviction. The team reveals the actual family's imperfect habits, persuading the building to want living tenants rather than manufactured ones. It evicts the predatory ghosts and becomes an affordable, occasionally judgmental rental.

pitches.title: The Disaster Rehearsal
pitches.text: Inside an abandoned factory, workers repeat a shift that ends in an explosion, each cycle spreading heat into nearby homes. The ghosts are trying different ways to prevent a disaster they cannot remember surviving. Engineering records show the owner escaped by locking a safety gate behind him. The investigators open the real gate outside the loop and guide the workers out through it. The factory finally burns cold, leaving enough evidence to destroy the owner's heroic reputation.

pitches.title: Empty for a Reason
pitches.text: The building's rooms are immaculate, except every reflection contains somebody running. The property was evacuated to contain a creature living in mirrored depth, and scavengers have removed the blinds that held it dormant. The team tracks a missing salvage worker between reflected rooms, retrieves him with a camera's delayed image, and clouds every surviving mirror. The creature retreats; the rescued worker must surrender his profitable collection of antique looking glasses.

pitches.title: The Building Is the Ghost
pitches.text: No one died in the abandoned school, yet its corridors moan and blackboards plead for attendance. Surveys reveal the demolished original school is haunting its own replacement site, reconstructing itself from alumni memories. Those memories now trap visitors as their childhood selves. The investigators hold one final alumni gathering outside, letting people mourn the place without wishing to return. It disappears peacefully, leaving the new development with an inexplicably excellent playground.

pitches.title: Squatter in the Foundation
pitches.text: The team enters an abandoned office and finds a gigantic sleeping face beneath its cellar. The building was constructed around an earth spirit, with vacant floors serving as insulation from human thought. An urban explorer's livestream is waking it into a furious image of its viewers' fears. The investigators stop the broadcast and tell the spirit one coherent reassuring story in person. It settles back to sleep, provided somebody occasionally visits without monetizing the encounter.

pitches.title: Unoccupied, Fully Staffed
pitches.text: The abandoned hotel has no guests but hundreds of unseen workers cleaning impossible rooms. A guestbook identifies them as guests who vanished after complaining about the staff. A vengeance spirit swapped their roles and now cannot distinguish guilt from bad manners. The investigators uncover the original mistreated maid's story and make the hotel owner finish a cleaning shift himself. The victims return, the spirit releases its punitive workforce, and the owner finally learns what a toilet brush does.

pitches.title: The Future Tenant
pitches.text: The abandoned building contains the investigators' own future offices, complete with memorial photographs of deceased colleagues. Messages describe a triumphant agency founded by sacrificing one team member here tonight. The offices are an ambitious psychic fungus projecting attractive futures to make its hosts stay. The team tests a minor prediction, catches the lie, and burns the growth before anyone accepts its promotion. They return to their car headquarters alive and distinctly less impressed by the promised benefits.

pitches.title: Asbestos Dragon
pitches.text: Hazard inspectors disappear inside an abandoned warehouse; thermal scans show something coiling around its beams. A juvenile dragon has eaten industrial insulation and now exhales toxic dust rather than fire. The team learns it is hoarding workers' hard hats because they resemble eggs. They recover the inspectors, exchange the hats for safe stone decoys, and lead the dragon to a sealed quarry for treatment. The property owner objects chiefly to losing the remaining insulation.

pitches.title: The House That Held the Line
pitches.text: An abandoned house fills with seawater despite standing inland, and its attic contains an elderly survivor's wartime distress signal. Her desperate promise to keep the sea away from town became a supernatural barrier anchored in the house. Now dying, she can no longer maintain it. With experts unreachable, the team helps neighbors build an ordinary flood diversion and releases her promise only after testing it. The sea recedes, and she finally gets to go home somewhere else.

title: Mall problem
description: Investigators requested to the local mall

pitches.title: The Food Court Afterlife
pitches.text: Customers cannot find the mall exit after ordering discontinued meals; employees see relatives in shuttered restaurants. A dead franchise owner has turned the food court into a cheap substitute afterlife, retaining souls who cannot afford the next passage. His debt collectors plan to repossess the living too. The investigators expose that passage was never priced, only falsely advertised, and open the loading dock to the true beyond. The owner follows last, carrying an unsold tray of nachos.

pitches.title: Mall Molting
pitches.text: Storefronts migrate overnight and shoppers emerge wearing living merchandise. The mall is the shell of a juvenile giant hermit creature, approaching its first molt with customers caught in the old layers. Reading the movements as anatomy lets the team predict the shedding route. They evacuate shoppers through the maintenance tunnels and lure the animal into an empty stadium. The landlord keeps the shed shell and immediately advertises it as a fresh retail opportunity.

pitches.title: The Sale That Ate Saturday
pitches.text: A clearance sale repeats until everyone buys something, while exhausted staff remember every iteration. A discount spell cast by a failing shopkeeper loops the day around total customer satisfaction, an impossible condition. The team finds one customer who cannot buy back a vanished childhood toy and helps them mourn it instead. Satisfaction stops meaning possession, the spell collapses, and the staff leave together before management can describe the extra shifts as voluntary.

pitches.title: Missing Mannequin
pitches.text: A mannequin disappears and several shoppers report being followed by someone with their exact posture. Security footage reveals mannequins rehearsing stolen lives to escape their display windows. A department store manager knowingly feeds them customers' images, intending to sell replacements to lonely families. The investigators offer the mannequins independent identities and paid work, separating liberation from impersonation. They release the copied customers; the manager discovers his new security guard remembers every insult he ever gave it.

pitches.title: Anchor Store
pitches.text: A closed department store pulls nearby shops toward it, stretching escalators and collapsing parking lanes. Its old nautical display contains an actual anchor from a ghost ship, and closure has broken the illusion that kept the vessel believing it was still at sea. The investigators reconstruct its final voyage from display labels and steer the spectral ship out through the decorative fountain. The mall survives, now short one anchor tenant in a much more literal sense.

pitches.title: The Loyalty Animal
pitches.text: Shoppers with old loyalty cards are stalked by a huge mascot that grows whenever they earn points. The mascot is a collective spirit of devotion fed by an abandoned rewards scheme; unredeemed points have become years of desperate expectation. The team sets up a real exchange for useful communal services, draining the accumulated promises. The mascot shrinks into a helpful little creature, finally receiving a reward itself: someone remembers its name and lets it rest.

pitches.title: Seasonal War
pitches.text: Halloween displays devour Christmas decorations, while Easter rabbits fortify the escalators. The mall's abandoned holiday rituals have awakened competing seasonal spirits, each trying to occupy the whole calendar. Store records reveal the conflict began when management demanded every season sell year-round. The investigators impose an ordinary schedule and hold one closing ceremony for the out-of-season beings. The seasonal truce survives because nobody wants to cover Black Friday, which becomes the staff's bargaining leverage.

pitches.title: The Fountain Takes Requests
pitches.text: Wishes tossed into the mall fountain come true by stealing equivalent good fortune from strangers. The investigators trace impossible promotions to sudden layoffs, then discover the fountain's trapped water spirit is bound to fulfill every coin. Draining it would release decades of unfinished wishes at once. They organize a final round of specific wishes to return what each beneficiary took. Freed from the backlog, the spirit departs; the fountain becomes blessedly useless indoor plumbing.

pitches.title: Unboxing the Predator
pitches.text: A package store receives boxes addressed to customers who have not ordered anything. Opening them produces an intimate perfect gift, followed by a mouth that demands the recipient enter. An extradimensional ambush predator has learned online shopping rituals from discarded packaging. The investigators find its nest in the return bins and flood it with deliberately unwanted gifts, causing the predator to reject its own bait. Customers escape while it sulks inside a giant box marked fragile.

pitches.title: Closing Time
pitches.text: At closing, forgotten shoppers are absorbed into murals depicting the mall's glory days. A retired security guard's ghost cannot accept that the place is dying, and preserves everybody he considers part of its history. The investigators enter the murals, find aging captives longing to leave, and bring the guard's estranged daughter to confront his false happy ending. He releases them and finishes his final patrol, allowing the mall to decline at an ordinary financially disastrous pace.

title: Strange catch
description: Local fishermen have caught something strange

pitches.title: The Fish With a Receipt
pitches.text: Fishermen catch a fish carrying receipts for purchases nobody remembers making. Following the receipts reveals a sea creature eating memories of tiny financial losses, gradually swallowing whole relationships attached to them. The fish is its digestive waste, not the monster itself. The investigators bait the creature with an honest communal account of unpaid debts, recover the trapped memories, and return it offshore. Several marriages survive, although the restored memories do not improve them.

pitches.title: The Man Who Swallowed the Hook
pitches.text: The catch is a living man whose lungs contain gills and whose pockets contain decades of missing wedding rings. He is a drowned fisherman transformed by a river spirit into its collector of broken promises. He demands the present crew fulfill promises they never made, flooding the harbor when they refuse. The team locates his widow, who releases him from his own vow to return. He dies human, the flood recedes, and the rings are finally reunited with their owners.

pitches.title: Small Catch, Big Mother
pitches.text: A translucent squid pulses with images of a vast shape beneath town. Every attempt to dissect it triggers earthquakes; sonar shows its mother wrapped around the continental shelf. The juvenile was separated by a deep-sea cable and is broadcasting distress through its captors' dreams. The investigators repair a route through the cable field and escort it offshore rather than wait for nonexistent military support. Its mother rises just long enough to make every boat captain reconsider their career.

pitches.title: Freshwater Future
pitches.text: A fish contains human-made plastic bearing next year's date, then spits up a drowned version of one investigator. The lake has begun draining a future flood backward through a snagged temporal current. Clues on the corpse identify the failed dam responsible. The team warns maintenance crews, cuts the obstruction in the lake, and repairs the dam in the present. The corpse disappears, but the investigator keeps its cheap watch as a deeply unpleasant scheduling aid.

pitches.title: Catch and Release and Release
pitches.text: The same huge fish is caught by different crews simultaneously, with each specimen insisting it is a human trapped by a witch. Testing their conflicting stories reveals that the fish multiply through sympathy, each rescue creating another hungry body. The supposed witch is a fisherman who accidentally gave a river trickster his name. The team restores his identity through his forgotten family nickname, collapsing the false victims into one ordinary fish that nobody feels especially guilty eating.

pitches.title: The Boat Egg
pitches.text: Fishermen net a leathery egg that vibrates whenever someone starts an engine. It hatches into a creature that thinks boats are its parents and nurses on fuel, sinking vessels as it grows. The investigators find similar eggs in old shipwrecks: the species reproduces around drowned timber, not people. They build it an uncrewed wooden raft, lure it away from the fleet, and return it to its spawning ground. The fishermen demand reimbursement for the unusually affectionate fuel theft.

pitches.title: Bottom Feeder
pitches.text: The strange catch is a knot of voices enclosed in a shell, begging not to be thrown back. Each voice belongs to someone drowned by the same successful fishing captain. The captain's bargain with a deep-water entity traded rivals for plentiful catches, but the evidence has finally grown a body. The team feeds the shell the captain's own confession, letting it identify its killer publicly. The entity collects him, and the sea yields the victims' remains instead of fish.

pitches.title: The Edible Island
pitches.text: The catch looks like a rock until cut sections grow grass, insects, and tiny houses. It is the seed of an oceanic island that roots wherever it bleeds; the harbor is rapidly turning into a miniature countryside. The team discovers its original island sank after careless extraction and returns every sold slice to a deep-water tray. The seed knits together and grows safely offshore, carrying a rescued seafood dealer who now owns the world's least accessible restaurant.

pitches.title: Weather in the Net
pitches.text: A fisherman hauls up a storm folded into the shape of a ray. Nearby pressure swings match its attempts to escape, and a private weather firm offers suspiciously generous hush money. The firm breeds storms and has lost control of a juvenile. The investigators expose its offshore hatchery and release the captured ray during its mother's passing front, ending the local damage. The rescued storm marks their car with one permanent personal raincloud, apparently as gratitude.

pitches.title: The Last Honest Fish Story
pitches.text: Every person who describes the strange catch causes it to become a larger, more terrifying animal. The investigators compare contradictory accounts and discover a story-eating spirit caught because the crew exaggerated an ordinary fish. Attempts to deny it only create a monstrous 'nothing.' They persuade the original fisherman to give a boring accurate account, including the undersized catch and illegal bait. The monster dwindles to a minnow, leaving a solved case and several very ordinary fishing fines.

title: Strange statue
description: An eerie statue has appeared over night

pitches.title: Monument to Tomorrow
pitches.text: The statue depicts an unknown woman rescuing the town, with an inscription dated next week. Interviews identify an ordinary cleaner who wants nothing to do with heroism; cracks in the statue predict injuries she has not suffered yet. A grateful future town has sent the memorial back, accidentally fixing her sacrificial death. The investigators break the pose and help her survive the coming flood another way. The bronze becomes a statue of several muddy people arguing over a rope.

pitches.title: The Sculptor Inside
pitches.text: The statue changes posture when nobody watches, and nearby artists lose their hands' coordination. An imprisoned sculptor spirit has built a body from stolen talent, but cannot complete its own face. The team tracks the theft to an uncredited apprentice erased from a famous master's history. They correct the public record and find her signed original work. Recognized at last, she abandons the stolen abilities and leaves the statue smiling with an entirely new face.

pitches.title: Pigeon King
pitches.text: Pigeons gather on the eerie statue, then begin delivering precise threats to the mayor. The figure is their collective ancestral spirit, awakened by demolition of the town's oldest nesting tower. Its demand for restitution becomes dangerous when it starts converting citizens into birds. The investigators locate surviving eggs in the demolition rubble and secure a replacement nesting site. The citizens return human, while the mayor must ceremonially inaugurate a building nobody can stop defecating on.

pitches.title: Unwelcome Return
pitches.text: The statue appears outside a retirement home; touching it restores youth but transfers every recovered year to another resident. It is a petrified age-eating spirit invited by a resident who regrets outliving her family. The investigators trace the accelerated deaths and discover the spirit itself is exhausted by immortality. They offer it the resident's willingly shared memories instead of more years. It dies as ordinary stone, and she remains old, alive, and unexpectedly less lonely.

pitches.title: The Town's Missing Face
pitches.text: Everybody recognizes the statue but cannot say whom it depicts. Documents show gaps where a founder's name should be; his erased face is returning after a spell hid his role in a historic massacre. Each attempted removal erases another witness. The investigators recover survivors' testimony and carve the victims' names around the statue, making memory collective rather than flattering. The town remembers its actual history, and the threatening monument becomes evidence instead of a hero.

pitches.title: Stone Migrant
pitches.text: The statue vanishes nightly and returns with muddy feet, apparently visiting every bus stop in town. Seismic readings reveal a stone-bodied species attempting to rejoin its herd after a collector imported it as sculpture. Its distress hardens pedestrians into temporary stone companions. The investigators follow its remembered route to a quarry full of 'statues,' release the herd, and escort their slow migration out of town. The collector reports a devastating loss of decorative assets.

pitches.title: The Idol That Wanted Out
pitches.text: A terrifying statue arrives with expensive offerings already at its feet. The team follows the donors to a cult whose god is trying to resign, sending its idol somewhere it hopes nobody worships. Unfortunately, the statue's ominous publicity recruits more believers. The investigators stage a humiliating but harmless display of its very limited powers and obtain the cult's disappointed consent to release it. The god becomes a local rock, delighted to receive no attention whatsoever.

pitches.title: Whose Statue Is It Anyway
pitches.text: The statue's face changes to whoever last complains about it, and that person starts committing the heroic deeds carved on its base. A civic spirit has mistaken public criticism for volunteering to improve the town. Escalating feats would force the latest critic to slay an actual underground beast. The team adds an achievable final deed—feeding everyone trapped by the crisis—and completes it together. The spirit accepts shared civic responsibility, leaving a monument with pleasantly indecisive features.

pitches.title: The Chisel Was a Tooth
pitches.text: Fresh stone dust appears around the statue, although the figure is getting larger. Quarry analysis reveals that it is a predator carving humanlike armor out of its mineral prey, preparing to pass among the town's sculptures before feeding on concrete foundations. The investigators lure it to a condemned parking structure, then collapse an uncontaminated stone enclosure around it. It settles into a mineral-rich sleep, saving town but creating the world's most consequential parking shortage.

pitches.title: Portrait of a Coward
pitches.text: The statue shows a trembling investigator holding a snapped weapon, although the team has never seen it before. Its base releases scenes from an alternate town where their counterparts died awaiting expert rescue. The statue is a warning sent by the one survivor, who founded an agency after the disaster. The team uses the recorded mistakes to avert the threat with improvised tools. The statue changes to an empty plinth, denying them a glorious memorial but confirming they live.

title: Sounds from the cave
description: Strange sounds are coming from a local cave

pitches.title: Hold Music Underground
pitches.text: The cave emits tinny hold music interrupted by requests to remain patient. Lost hikers' phones show calls connected decades ago; a blind burrowing spirit feeds on suspended anticipation, keeping callers alive and waiting beneath the rock. The investigators locate its throat by following the audio delay. They tell the captives that nobody is coming, prompting them to hang up and escape together. The spirit starves, while the team returns to a headquarters line playing nearly identical music.

pitches.title: The Mountain's Toothache
pitches.text: The cave groans every time quarry workers blast nearby, and fallen rocks resemble enormous teeth. The mountain is a sleeping organism whose infected tooth has become the cave. Its pain shakes homes apart, while well-meaning cultists worsen it with offerings lodged in the wound. The investigators recruit a very startled quarry crew to clear the infection and seal the exposed root. The mountain settles, leaving the foreman to invoice for the largest dental procedure in history.

pitches.title: Applause in the Dark
pitches.text: Applause comes from a sealed chamber whenever somebody lies near the cave. A forgotten comedian's ghost performs for an audience of creatures nourished by false hope; its next joke promises rescue to trapped hikers and draws them deeper. The investigators recover the performer's final honest routine, about dying broke and being afraid. He performs it, the false audience dissolves, and the hikers escape. The ghost finally receives genuine applause from people who would rather be anywhere else.

pitches.title: The Earth's First Baby
pitches.text: Crying from the cave is accompanied by sudden eruptions of flowers and confused newborn animals. An ancient life spirit is giving birth, but modern runoff has poisoned its nesting pool and its contractions are creating incompatible creatures. The investigators trace and divert the contamination, then guide the parent toward clean groundwater. A new guardian emerges harmlessly, while the improvised cleanup crew receives congratulations instead of the hazard pay they actually wanted.

pitches.title: Echoes With Teeth
pitches.text: The cave repeats voices with new words, and hikers obey instructions they swear they gave themselves. A colony of sound-bodied predators builds convincing personalities from echoes, then lures the originals into deep shafts. The investigators notice that voices cannot describe anything said in absolute silence. Using written instructions and hand signals, they retrieve captives and break the chamber's resonance with irregular rubble. The surviving echoes continue arguing, but nobody mistakes them for useful professional advice.

pitches.title: Understudy Apocalypse
pitches.text: The cave broadcasts rehearsals for the end of the world, complete with someone repeatedly apologizing for missed cues. Inside, minor demons are preparing a catastrophe their absent supervisor never authorized because the hierarchy has collapsed. Their mistakes are already creating local fissures. The team proves the supervising demon was destroyed long ago and offers the performers an ordinary outdoor production instead. The infernal apparatus is dismantled for stage equipment, while one understudy demands a better dressing room.

pitches.title: Songs of the Missing River
pitches.text: The cave sings names of townspeople shortly before they sleepwalk toward it. Water maps reveal a diverted river spirit calling descendants of the workers who imprisoned it underground. It intends to dissolve them into tributaries and restore its course through town. The investigators uncover the old riverbed and arrange a safe partial return, trading restoration for the captives. The spirit accepts a narrower river, although several homeowners must become much more enthusiastic about waterfront living.

pitches.title: Recording Failure
pitches.text: Sounds inside the cave match conversations the investigators have not yet had, including a colleague's dying apology. The cave is a natural chamber that echoes possible futures; fearful listeners choose the predicted path and make it real. The team tests it with a trivial deliberately changed decision, then refuses the fatal rescue sequence it predicts. They recover the trapped colleague by an unrecorded route and close the entrance, keeping one ugly argument that would otherwise have remained unsaid.

pitches.title: The Sleeping Chorus
pitches.text: The cave hums in the voices of deceased townspeople, attracting mourners who vanish overnight. They are joining a fungal consciousness that absorbed buried bodies and can reproduce their memories accurately, but cannot release a living guest intact. The investigators discover the network recoils from fresh daylight and open a ventilation shaft. The living stagger out as the dead memories fade, forcing the town to choose mortal grief over an eternal reunion that ate its participants.

pitches.title: A Very Large Dog
pitches.text: Scratching and whining come from a cave too small for the shadow moving inside. A local child's missing imaginary dog has grown for every lonely year its creator forgot it, wedging itself between worlds. Attempts to drag it out bring fragments of dangerous imaginary predators too. The investigators reunite the adult owner with it and ask her to imagine a manageable size. The creature emerges as a normal-sized, thoroughly impossible dog that immediately demands its overdue walk.

title: Cat problem
description: Investigators requested to the local cat cafe

pitches.title: Nine Lives, One Customer
pitches.text: A regular at the cat cafe is caught dying and returning every afternoon, while one cat becomes increasingly frail. The cafe's founder accidentally bound the animal's nine lives to her suicidal widower through a protective wish. His attempts to test immortality are spending them rapidly. The investigators show him the cat's suffering, help him accept care, and reverse the bond with his consent. Both survive on one ordinary life, and he inherits daily feeding duty.

pitches.title: The Cats Are the Staff
pitches.text: Customers complain that the barista changes face while every cat seems to know their order. A broke witch turned exhausted cafe workers into cats so they could rest, but their wages remain locked in human accounts. The owner has begun hiring replacements without informing them. The investigators recover the workers' identities through their individual routines and undo the transformation. The reunited staff negotiate humane schedules, retaining one voluntary afternoon each week of sleeping in the window.

pitches.title: Something in the Milk
pitches.text: Cafe cats stare at a refrigerator that begins purring back; vanished deliveries reappear as tiny cat-shaped people. A house spirit has adopted the cafe and is converting everything inside into what it thinks the owners love most. The investigators identify its loneliness beneath the transformations and give it a distinct name and a place of its own. Recognized without becoming a cat, it releases its altered guests and becomes the cafe's deeply protective pantry.

pitches.title: Cafe at the End of Life
pitches.text: Cats begin escorting customers into a back room that does not exist on the floor plan. Inside are deceased relatives offering final conversations, but visitors who stay too long cannot return. The cats are natural guides whose usual route has been disrupted by renovations. The investigators restore their hidden threshold and retrieve a customer who mistakes closure for reunion. The cafe keeps a harmless farewell ritual, with the staff firmly enforcing its surprisingly important time limit.

pitches.title: The Big Cat
pitches.text: One cafe kitten eats nothing yet grows larger whenever customers say it is adorable. Photographs reveal an ancient predatory spirit disguised as whatever humans most wish to protect. Its eventual adult form will devour the neighborhood. The investigators find its original portrait and circulate an honest account of what it is, breaking the collective fantasy. It dwindles to a grouchy stone idol, which the owner keeps behind glass because customers still think the ears are charming.

pitches.title: The Missing Shadow
pitches.text: The cats have no shadows, and human customers begin shedding theirs after being scratched. An apprentice magician hid a shadow-eating creature inside the cafe's new scratching post; the cats are starving it by keeping the shadows pinned under furniture. The team retrieves the apprentice's binding materials and returns each stolen shadow before removing the creature. The cats receive no credit for containing a catastrophe, but do obtain an extremely expensive replacement scratching post.

pitches.title: Adoption Interview
pitches.text: Every adopted cat returns to the cafe carrying its new owner's worst memory, leaving that person dangerously fearless. The cafe sits above a dreaming predator, and the cats have been feeding it nightmares to keep it asleep. The adoption boom is awakening it through overfeeding. The investigators restore the owners' memories, close the tunnel, and move the cafe beyond the creature's reach. The predator wakes into an empty basement and finds nobody worth pursuing.

pitches.title: The Queen's Retirement
pitches.text: An elderly cat receives visitors who bow, leave pearls, and occasionally fail to look human. She is a faerie ruler who fled court to enjoy being pampered; rival claimants start turning cafe patrons into pawns for a succession war. The investigators obtain her explicit abdication, witnessed by every rival, and insist that citizenship does not extend to customers. The war departs with the succession, while the former queen remains a spoiled cat and finally stops holding grudges for centuries.

pitches.title: Cat Copy Machine
pitches.text: The cafe's cat count doubles nightly, but each newcomer has one disturbing human habit. The founder's dead cat is reincarnating through lonely visitors, pulling their personalities into new bodies while the visitors grow vacant. The investigators find its ashes inside the espresso machine and separate them from the water supply. They let the original spirit inhabit one living kitten with no borrowed human mind. The duplicates vanish, the customers recover, and the espresso is noticeably less affectionate.

pitches.title: The Mouse Was Right
pitches.text: All the cats hide from a single ordinary-looking mouse, while cups move themselves and the owner insists nothing is wrong. The mouse is a sorcerer whom the owner hired to increase foot traffic; it has seized her body and is secretly replacing customers with obedient mice. The team trusts the cats' evidence, traps the mouse without harming its human prisoners, and forces a reversal. The owner returns, cancels her promotion, and discovers the cats expect payment for the rescue.

title: Mysterious car
description: A strange car has been causing trouble around town

pitches.title: The Driver Who Never Arrived
pitches.text: A car appears outside homes shortly before their owners vanish. Its radio repeats an old hitchhiker's unanswered request, and its trunk contains the luggage of people who abandoned others during emergencies. The vehicle is driven by the ghost of a stranded woman, forcing each target to experience her fatal journey. The investigators locate her remains and the actual driver who left her. She releases the lesser offenders and takes him on one final ride that does not return.

pitches.title: Carpool with Yourself
pitches.text: The mysterious car delivers people to destinations they considered visiting years ago; they return with memories of different lives. An inventor's navigation device has become attached to a regret-eating creature, turning roads into alternate histories. The investigator who wants to stay finds the borrowed life displacing someone else's actual existence. The team retrieves the stranded travelers and disconnects the device at its original abandoned junction, choosing their imperfect lives over stealing better ones.

pitches.title: The Hungry Hatchback
pitches.text: The car steals vehicles' fuel without opening their tanks, then starts drinking warmth from pedestrians. It is a newborn mechanical organism assembled from a junkyard haunted by scrapped vehicles. The investigators notice it follows service vans, seeking someone to repair a cracked energy organ. They patch it with salvage and teach it to absorb harmless solar heat. The creature settles into their fleet, a useful company car with an alarming habit of licking charging stations.

pitches.title: Road Rage Incarnate
pitches.text: Witnesses describe different cars but identical aggressive driving, and each encounter leaves the victim obsessed with pursuing it. A road spirit has formed from decades of rage at a fatal interchange, possessing the angriest nearby driver. Every chase strengthens it. The investigators trace its first death and close the dangerous lane while confronting the grieving family. When traffic stops reenacting that crash, the spirit disperses, leaving several furious drivers with nobody supernatural to blame.

pitches.title: Passenger Seat Vacant
pitches.text: The car drives itself politely until someone sits in the passenger seat, after which their body stays home while their voice comes from the radio. A lonely transport spirit steals company rather than flesh, holding minds for endless conversation. The team interviews its passengers and discovers it will accept a willing finite journey. One investigator rides with it to the edge of town, hears its old loss, and ends the conversation kindly. The minds return, and the car stops collecting replacements.

pitches.title: The Hearse of Unfinished Business
pitches.adjustment: The car is an unmarked vintage hearse.
pitches.text: The vehicle blocks streets near people pretending their dead relatives left no obligations. Inside its coffin lie tasks, not bodies: an unfinished apology, an unreturned loan, an abandoned dog. A funeral driver's ghost has been trying to complete his clients' last wishes, and exhaustion is making him indiscriminate. The investigators finish the genuine tasks and identify fabricated ones planted by a greedy beneficiary. The driver finally rests, leaving an excellent hearse and terrible resale prospects.

pitches.title: Model Year Impossible
pitches.text: The car's registration lists a manufacturer that will not exist for thirty years. Its occupant is a future repo agent reclaiming vehicles whose owners supposedly defaulted, including a toddler's future first car. The debt projections are feeding a temporal parasite that makes hypothetical failure real. The investigators destroy its predictive ledger while keeping evidence of actual current ownership. The repossessions reverse, the future firm loses its foundation, and the agent must find a very present-day job.

pitches.title: The Paint That Moves
pitches.text: A sports car's paint reflects a driver although the seat is empty, and photographed reflections begin wandering out of other vehicles. A muralist trapped inside magical pigment is spreading escape routes through every reflected image, unintentionally releasing less friendly painted beings. The team locates the mural he was torn from and brings the car alongside it. He exits into the original artwork, reseals the fleeing figures, and leaves the proud owner with wonderfully ordinary primer.

pitches.title: One More Mile
pitches.text: The mysterious car gives hitchhikers amazing luck until its odometer reaches another milestone, when somebody they love dies. Its engine was bound to a gambler's demon that converts traveled distance into wagers against passengers' happiness. The investigators reconstruct the pattern from accident reports and find the demon cannot take what is freely risked on no reward. They tow it through the final mile as an act of rescue, exhausting its wager and leaving a very tired, unenchanted car.

pitches.title: The Town That Was the Driver
pitches.text: The car appears at every blocked development project, crashes construction equipment, and always escapes unoccupied. Its tire dirt matches every part of town: it is the settlement's collective survival instinct, acting through a beloved retired taxi. The investigators discover it is attacking repairs as well as destructive development because it cannot distinguish change from loss. They guide it through a tour of necessary improvements, teaching it the difference. It becomes an unusually selective traffic-calming service.

title: Weird vending machine
description: A local vending machine doesn’t have the normal stock

pitches.title: Lost and Dispensed
pitches.text: The machine sells items customers lost years ago, from house keys to a vanished wedding ring. A purchase history shows it is retrieving things from wherever they currently exist, including evidence and eventually missing people. Its cheerful display conceals a scavenger spirit with no concept of ownership. The investigators reunite a retrieved person with her actual family, show it the damage caused by indiscriminate returns, and restrict its offerings to unclaimed possessions. Its best seller becomes mismatched socks.

pitches.title: Tomorrow's Lunch
pitches.text: Snacks contain dated notes in customers' own handwriting, predicting little disasters that keep coming true. The machine is communicating with its future self, stealing food and warnings from an abandoned disaster shelter. Opening the casing reveals tomorrow's shelter is inside the investigators' future headquarters. They avert the recorded gas explosion and sever the feed, preventing both deaths and an organization built around exploiting future tragedy. Their refund arrives as an ordinary packet of stale crackers.

pitches.title: Actual Courage
pitches.text: A machine vends courage, patience, and charisma as flavored drinks, while customers develop the opposite traits after the effects wear off. It extracts each virtue from somebody nearby and cycles it among buyers, concentrating fear into one unfortunate janitor. The investigators map the exchanges and pour all remaining drinks back into the supply reservoir. Everyone regains their own imperfect temperament, the janitor recovers, and the machine can only vend water marketed as adequate self-confidence.

pitches.title: Small Gods, Exact Change
pitches.text: The machine dispenses thumb-sized gods who grant tiny favors and demand increasingly personal offerings. An ancient pantheon was trapped in convenience-store packaging after losing its worshippers; every sale begins rebuilding a domain. The investigators discover one forgotten god of departures can open the original prison if thanked sincerely. They help the miniature deities leave together rather than compete for customers. The machine empties, and one escaped god stays voluntarily to protect bus-stop benches.

pitches.title: The Meal That Ate You
pitches.text: The machine sells beautifully packaged meals that whisper diners' private worries. People who finish them disappear; their names appear as new flavors on the menu. A shapeshifting carnivore offers comfort food made from the memories of previous victims, digesting consumers into its next invitation. The team refuses the perfect meal, breaks the refrigeration enchantment, and pulls partially digested customers from warming packets. The creature escapes as a bland sandwich, which a fearless investigator promptly incinerates.

pitches.title: Refund in Years
pitches.text: Customers receive old versions of themselves instead of refunds, and the doubles try to reclaim the lives they believe were stolen. A time spirit inhabits the machine's return slot, interpreting buyer's remorse as permission to reverse personal history. The investigators find the first customer whose regret taught it the idea and help him distinguish disappointment from theft. He accepts his actual life and closes the original refund request; every temporal double merges safely with its present self.

pitches.title: The Machine Is Homesick
pitches.text: The vending machine offers impossible minerals and food that makes customers breathe strange gases. It is a living supply pod stranded from an alien survey team, trying to prepare friendly locals for its toxic home atmosphere. Their transformations are its earnest thank-you gifts. The investigators decipher its nutrition labels, reverse the treatments with its emergency stock, and build a signal from its unusual products. Its rescuers return for it and leave a case of safely boring human snacks.

pitches.title: Out of Stock, Out of Luck
pitches.text: The machine dispenses miniature emergencies: a house fire in a jar, a broken engagement in a box. Destroying a package prevents the event, but buying too many makes unsold disasters happen immediately to strangers. A retired oracle trapped tomorrow's possibilities here to avoid making judgments himself. The investigators free the oracle from his self-imposed hiding place and make him distribute warnings openly. The dangerous products dissolve into information, leaving choices with the people who must live them.

pitches.title: Exact Change Only
pitches.text: Customers can buy priceless treasures, but the coin slot rejects money and accepts fingernails, baby teeth, and eventually voices. The machine is an old faerie exchange whose listed prices faded long ago. The investigators recover the original price markings and discover the operator has been charging for wishes nobody requested. They demand a fair audit under the exchange's own binding promise, return the stolen pieces, and shut it down. Their hard-won compensation is one spectacularly useless crown.

pitches.title: The Employee Break Room
pitches.text: A machine appears wherever exhausted workers take breaks and sells an hour of perfect rest for a dollar. Its users wake rejuvenated, but another unseen workforce is aging in their place. A dream merchant has imprisoned its own former customers as attendants in the peaceful retreat. The investigators enter, organize the attendants' escape, and replace the stolen rest with freely shared quiet time. The merchant loses its captive labor, and the physical machine finally dispenses coffee that merely tastes bad.

title: Weird meme
description: Investigators requested to figure out what the kids are on about

pitches.title: You Had to Be There
pitches.text: Kids insist a phrase is hilarious, but explaining it causes adults to lose a day of memory. The team finds the joke is a fragment of an erased event, spread by a trapped teenage ghost trying to make witnesses remember. Her death was covered up during a school trip. The investigators recover the full account and publish it without the enchanted phrase. The ghost passes on, the missing days return, and the kids complain the adults have ruined the joke.

pitches.title: The Reaction Face
pitches.text: A meme's grinning face begins appearing in mirrors, while users find they cannot stop smiling. Comparing old copies reveals the face is a mimic learning human expression through millions of reactions; it mistakes involuntary joy for safe social belonging. The team posts an unfiltered account of fear, grief, and exhaustion, giving it a fuller emotional vocabulary. It releases the trapped faces and chooses one ordinary human disguise, which begins an awkward but honest life offline.

pitches.title: Tag Your Replacement
pitches.text: A tagging trend generates flattering cartoon doubles, and tagged kids start missing classes while the cartoons attend for them. A dream artist sells ideal selves to an audience that would rather not cope with real teenagers. The investigators follow imperfect details omitted from each drawing into the artist's studio and recover the originals. They make the doubles encounter the problems their perfection cannot solve, dissolving the fantasy. Parents have to accept their returned, thoroughly inconvenient actual children.

pitches.title: The Joke That Cannot Land
pitches.text: Each retelling of the meme produces a small impossible accident, and the final punchline is always obscured. Its author glimpsed a cosmic trickster whose complete joke would make causality collapse. The kids are unknowingly assembling the missing lines from different uploads. The team identifies a harmless deliberately bad ending and makes that version spread first. The trickster accepts collective groaning as its payoff, stabilizes the accidents, and departs deeply satisfied by everyone's disappointment.

pitches.title: The Meme Is a Map
pitches.text: Kids copy an absurd dance and begin vanishing at the same final step. Motion analysis reveals the sequence is a map through folded space, accidentally recovered from an alien distress beacon. The missing kids are stranded inside a failing station, not kidnapped. The investigators learn the sequence, use household supplies to signal the exits, and lead them back before the station collapses. The survivors release a safer dance ending, though nobody wants to hear the adults' rescue story.

pitches.title: Offline Challenge
pitches.text: A meme dares followers to turn off their phones simultaneously; every participant hears a voice naming them. An attention-starved entity lives in the gaps between electronic signals, using coordinated silence to regain a body. The investigators trace the campaign to a kid whose missing brother now speaks through it. They retrieve the brother from the silence with a battery-powered beacon and interrupt the synchronized blackout. The entity dissolves, leaving a perfectly reasonable argument about screen time unresolved.

pitches.title: Please Do Not Perceive Me
pitches.text: Kids share a blurred creature captioned with pleas to ignore it, and each new view erases another part of its body. It is a living being cursed to become what observers expect, using humor to convince people it ought not exist. Its disappearance begins erasing everything it once touched, including a child's life. The investigators establish its actual history and spread truthful images instead of interpretations. It stabilizes in its own form and finally gets to stop performing relatability.

pitches.title: The Sponsored Curse
pitches.text: The meme grants spectacular luck after users repeat a slogan, but the luck funnels their lives toward a mysterious local warehouse. There, a failing brand has hired a prosperity spirit to turn customers into product spokespeople permanently. The team discovers the slogan promises affection the brand cannot deliver and documents that breach in a viral parody. The bond breaks, the captive promoters escape, and the spirit repossesses the warehouse rather than the customers.

pitches.title: An Ancient Bad Post
pitches.text: A crude image resurfaces every time somebody tries to delete it, dragging ancient architecture into the surrounding street. It is the last surviving fragment of a civilization erased by collective shame, and public mockery is reconstructing the disaster that destroyed it. The investigators find its original context in a surviving tomb and reveal it was a terrified plea for help, not a joke. Genuine recognition stops the repetition, and the resurrected street settles into harmless archaeological evidence.

pitches.title: Everyone Is Doing It
pitches.text: The supposed meme has no image, phrase, or action, yet kids insist everybody understands. Interviews reveal a telepathic adolescent creature borrowing social certainty from its classmates to hide its complete confusion about human life. Its growing network begins overwriting dissenting personalities. The investigators persuade one confident student to admit they do not understand, freeing the others to do the same. The network breaks, and the creature becomes merely another confused kid whom the school must actually support.

title: Community college problem
description: Investigators are requested to the local community college

pitches.title: Introduction to Necromancy
pitches.text: A continuing-education class promises help with unfinished projects, and deceased former students turn up carrying homework. The instructor revived their determination without reviving their bodies, creating ghosts doomed to complete courses they cannot pass. The investigators inspect transcripts and discover the school retroactively raised the graduation requirements. They restore the original credits, let the dead finish their actual obligations, and close the class. The instructor admits resurrection sounded easier than fixing the student database.

pitches.title: Transfer Credit from Elsewhere
pitches.text: Students transfer into classes that teach impossible histories and emerge with memories of alien childhoods. The registrar accidentally established an exchange program with another universe through a misfiled astronomical chart. Both campuses are merging as students accumulate incompatible credits. The team traces individual enrollment paths, arranges safe reciprocal transfers, and destroys the overlapping course map. Everyone returns to the right universe, though a few insist the other one offered much better parking.

pitches.title: The Forever Student
pitches.text: One adult student has attended for forty years without aging, and classmates who tutor him lose months overnight. He bargained with a learning spirit never to graduate because education was the only place he felt valued. The spirit is taking years from everyone helping him stay unfinished. The investigators find the career he once abandoned, support a first real step toward it, and convince him to complete his last course. He ages naturally, and his classmates get their stolen time back.

pitches.title: Vocational Possession
pitches.text: Trade students display expert skills overnight but also compulsive habits belonging to dead professionals. New training mannequins contain ghosts donated by a sinister apprenticeship program that treats possession as employability. The ghosts are slowly replacing the students they meant to help. The investigators reunite each ghost with an unfinished earthly task, letting them share expertise voluntarily before departing. The students keep what they genuinely learned, and the department must teach the rest at its ordinary understaffed pace.

pitches.title: The Basement Thesis
pitches.text: The campus basement expands around an impossible machine built by an adjunct whose research was dismissed for years. It manifests any theory his committee rejects, and academic disagreement is assembling contradictory universes above the cafeteria. The team reads his notes and discovers the machine responds to humiliation rather than truth. They secure an honest review acknowledging his work and its failures, allowing him to shut it down without vindication through catastrophe. His overdue payment remains a less solvable problem.

pitches.title: Attendance Required
pitches.text: Absentees wake in their classroom regardless of distance, and the empty campus fills after midnight with terrified former students. A safety charm created after a fatal dropout has attached survival to attendance, dragging everyone who ever enrolled into perpetual protection. The investigators identify the grieving teacher who bound it and show her living graduates who thrived after leaving. She withdraws the promise of compulsory safety; the students return home, some still determined to skip the next class.

pitches.title: The Career Counselor Knows
pitches.text: The career center accurately assigns students jobs that do not yet exist, then shapes accidents to make those careers necessary. Its new counselor is a fate parasite feeding on fulfilled professional destinies, arranging disasters to produce demand for rescuers and mourners. The investigators compare appointment records with incidents and organize students to choose unpredicted paths together. The parasite loses its map of the future and departs, leaving the center to admit that nobody can guarantee employment.

pitches.title: Campus for Sale
pitches.text: The college receives an irresistible acquisition offer, but representatives have no shadows and brochures depict students as livestock. A faerie entrepreneur intends to buy the campus as a breeding ground for highly trained servants, exploiting a founder's ancient land bargain. The investigators uncover a clause returning the land when learning serves the community without profit. Students provide a free public workshop, triggering the release and voiding the sale. The college survives through a practical service it already knew how to perform.

pitches.title: Remedial Existence
pitches.text: Students in a new remedial class disappear from records while continuing to attend. The instructor is a forgotten god of beginnings, trying to give struggling adults a clean start by erasing everything that came before. Without a past, they cannot maintain a stable present and begin fading. The investigators collect their inconvenient histories from family and classmates, restore them publicly, and teach the god that starting again means carrying experience forward. Nobody gets a perfect transcript, but everybody exists.

pitches.title: The Student Body
pitches.text: Campus clubs start behaving like organs, with the debate society breathing for the athletics team and the cafeteria developing a literal pulse. A communal spirit has taken the promise of one student body literally after a donor ritual. The growing organism will absorb anyone who fails to fit its assigned function. The investigators help clubs deliberately collaborate across those assignments, demonstrating a community can cooperate without becoming one creature. The spirit dissolves into ordinary shared enthusiasm and several canceled donor plaques.

title: Problem at the amusement park
description: Investigators are requested to the local amusement park

pitches.title: The Ride Remembers
pitches.text: A roller coaster repeats a fatal derailment for passengers who cannot get off, while park staff dismiss the screams as atmosphere. Its trapped operator is rehearsing every safety decision, convinced a perfect run can undo the accident. The investigators recover the tampered maintenance report proving the fault was outside his control. He accepts that responsibility is not omnipotence and halts the loop. The passengers escape, and the park's owner finally faces the consequence he outsourced to a ghost.

pitches.title: Mascot on Strike
pitches.text: The park mascot refuses to remove its head, and costumed workers are turning into the animals they portray. The costumes contain minor spirits hired to animate the park's brand, neglected after their handlers were dismissed. Their protest is spreading involuntary transformation across guests. The investigators locate the original handlers and mediate a return of care rather than corporate ownership. Workers regain their bodies, while the spirits leave together to form an attraction with considerably less humiliating choreography.

pitches.title: The Queue Beyond Death
pitches.text: A new ride has a line that never shortens, and people who wait vanish from the park map. The queue passes into an unfinished afterlife where a stranded ferryman has disguised his crossing as an attraction to recruit living passengers. The team follows abandoned shoes through the hidden route and repairs his broken vessel. The living leave the line, the dead finally cross, and the park must explain why its most popular attraction was technically a transportation emergency.

pitches.title: Height Requirement
