pitches.text: Short children grow tall enough for every ride, then keep growing until the park's roofs split. An old giant granted a desperate park owner's wish that no visitor ever be too small, feeding growth with years stolen from adults. The investigators find the literal wish in a buried opening-day capsule and ask the owner to withdraw it rather than demand another correction. Children and adults recover, while the giant departs disappointed that humans cannot state a sensible request once.

pitches.title: Tunnel of Actual Love
pitches.text: Couples leave the tunnel knowing each other perfectly, then slowly become one shared person. A lonely water spirit thinks love means eliminating every difference and has begun joining passengers physically. The investigators find an elderly couple whose affection survives genuine disagreement and bring them through together. Their example reveals intimacy without erasure, prompting the spirit to separate its victims. The tunnel remains mildly romantic, mostly because neither partner can see the peeling paint in the dark.

pitches.title: The Best Day of Your Life
pitches.text: Guests refuse to leave and recall increasingly perfect childhoods; their families remember them dying in unrelated accidents. The park feeds on nostalgia, offering ideal revisions while consuming each guest's real life. The investigators find the oldest attendant trapped inside a memory of opening day and recover his imperfect original account. Sharing that account breaks the park's promise of perfection. Guests reclaim their actual histories and escape; the attraction survives as an ordinary disappointing amusement park.

pitches.title: The Prize Wants to Go Home
pitches.text: Carnival prizes cry at night and sabotage games until children win them. They are transformed animals taken from a faerie woodland, trying to escape through adoption; once home, their curse spreads to households. The investigators trace stitched tags to the trapper's warehouse and retrieve the animals' stolen names. Speaking them restores the creatures and releases affected families. They return the animals to the wood, leaving the park with inexpensive prizes nobody can accuse of having souls.

pitches.title: Ferris Wheel of Fortune
pitches.text: The wheel gives riders glimpses of fabulous futures, followed by desperate demands that they repeat the ride. Its axle turns through possible worlds, stealing favorable outcomes from unseen versions of passengers. Those ruined counterparts begin arriving to reclaim their lives. The investigators stop the wheel between advertised destinations, open both sides, and reconcile choices before returning everyone to their own world. The wheel becomes ordinary again, and nobody is pleased to pay full price for the limited view.

pitches.title: Fireworks Rehearsal
pitches.text: Nightly fireworks form increasingly accurate maps of the town burning. The pyrotechnician inherited powders that contain captive fire spirits, whose performance rehearses their planned escape. The investigators notice the finale outlines the park's evacuation routes and find the spirits' original river-bound home. They replace the finale with a guided route into water, freeing the beings without igniting the town. The audience calls it disappointing, while the team quietly accepts a very good review from the fire department.

pitches.title: The Park Under the Park
pitches.text: A maintenance crew finds a second amusement park buried beneath the first, staffed by silent copies of missing visitors. The older park is a carnivorous landscape growing a reassuring surface to lure prey downward. Copies struggle to warn the team because they carry fragments of the swallowed people. The investigators use those fragments to locate living captives and rescue them, then sever the surface from its feeding roots. The survivor copies become independent people with unsettlingly cheerful customer-service voices.

title: Missing business
description: A cherished local business has vanished without a trace

pitches.title: The Shop That Took a Holiday
pitches.text: A beloved bakery vanishes, leaving a warm loaf in the middle of its empty lot. Flour trails and late deliveries reveal the building grew into a protective spirit through generations of care; after its owner collapsed, it carried her away to rest. The team tracks it to a quiet hillside and explains that disappearing has made her worry worse. They organize neighbors to cover her work, and the bakery returns once she believes she can stop without losing everything.

pitches.title: Nobody Ever Worked There
pitches.text: The missing shop remains vivid in customers' memories, but nobody recalls a worker's name. It was operated by an entity that fed on being needed, slowly trading its own identity for perfect service until it vanished completely. The investigators find old staff photographs hidden behind anonymous thank-you notes and recover the proprietor's actual history. Publicly recognizing him as a person rebuilds the shop. He returns with boundaries, shorter hours, and a sign explaining that beloved is not a wage.

pitches.title: The Rival Bought the Location
pitches.text: A familiar hardware store disappears and its regular customers develop holes in their home repairs. A rival bought the place's magical 'location' from a land spirit, relocating every effect the business ever had along with the building. The investigators trace the missing repairs to a pristine new development containing impossible structures. They recover the store's original foundation stone and return it, restoring the borrowed history. The rival keeps his legal purchase of a now thoroughly useless empty parcel.

pitches.title: Last Call Somewhere Else
pitches.adjustment: The business is a neighborhood bar.
pitches.text: The bar vanishes while its neon sign continues glowing in reflections. Its dead founder made it sanctuary for anyone who truly had nowhere to go, and one customer's despair has pulled the whole building outside the world. The team enters through a reflected doorway and finds patrons happy but unable to leave. They arrange actual shelter for the stranded customer, reducing the need that anchors the bar. It returns, keeping its generous policy and considerably more realistic local partnerships.

pitches.title: The Business Outlived Its Town
pitches.text: The vanished store's receipts now name a town demolished a century ago. Renovation broke a spell that let the store survive its original settlement by pretending the present town was the same place. Its elderly owner has been knowingly maintaining that illusion to avoid losing everyone again. The investigators find descendants of her old neighbors and help her create new relationships without false continuity. The store returns in a changed form, and she finally retires from preserving an entire century alone.

pitches.title: Inventory of a Life
pitches.text: The beloved repair shop vanishes, followed by memories of everything its owner fixed. He sold his accumulated usefulness to a demon to pay for lifesaving treatment, inadvertently including the premises. The investigators reconstruct his work from unrepaired objects and show the demon that many repairs were gifts it never legally purchased. They reclaim those shared contributions, giving the owner and building a stable foothold. His treatment remains paid, while the demon reluctantly keeps only a drawer of genuinely billable parts.

pitches.title: The Closing Sale Worked
pitches.text: A cherished bookstore advertised that everything must go; by morning its building, staff, and customers have gone too. A dormant word spirit inhabiting the last unsold dictionary interpreted the desperate announcement literally. The team tracks handwritten sale signs into an empty language-space where the missing people are becoming definitions. They cross out the owner's claim that nobody cares and replace it with truthful requests for help. The store returns, saved by real support rather than a magically profitable slogan.

pitches.title: Franchise of One
pitches.text: The business disappears after rejecting a franchise offer, while identical branches arise in neighboring towns overnight. An expanding commercial organism has consumed the original to copy its charm, preserving the owner inside its central kitchen. The investigators follow slight imperfections that the copies cannot reproduce, locate the captive, and broadcast his refusal to the entire network. Without his identity, the artificial charm collapses. He escapes with the original shop, while the empty branches become ordinary properties investors must actually maintain.

pitches.title: Open in the Other World
pitches.text: The storefront vanishes, but online orders still arrive in packages smelling of unfamiliar rain. Its owner inadvertently accepted a faerie delivery contract whose exclusive territory included the whole building. Customers are delighted, unaware that each order binds a worker more tightly to the other world. The investigators enter through a returned parcel, document that earthly customers never consented to the relocation, and invoke the contract's mutual-service condition. The shop returns, and the workers receive their withheld earnings in negotiably real money.

pitches.title: The Town Forgot to Ask
pitches.text: The cherished business vanishes and every resident remembers a different version: bakery, diner, cobbler, cinema. It was a shape-changing being offering whichever place each visitor most needed, slowly exhausted by contradictory demands. The investigators find it collapsed in the unrecognized space between their memories. They ask what it wants for the first time and help it choose one stable identity: a quiet tea shop. It returns smaller, less universally beloved, and finally able to close on Mondays.
